recommendations.section: ## 2. Project Ideas by ECE Domain (### 2.6 Power electronics and energy)
recommendations.current: Texas Instruments' application notes give an unusually complete design path. SLVA477 provides the step-by-step power-stage equations: maximum duty cycle D = VOUT/(VIN(max) × η), inductor sizing for 20–40% ripple current, diode and capacitor selection [[application-note-2]]. SLVA432 walks through Type-III compensation for a synchronous buck converter, targeting a crossover near fSW/5 with about 60° phase margin, with measured efficiency up to 95% on its reference design [[application-report]]. The classic SLVA057 derives the buck power stage's steady-state and small-signal behaviour in both continuous and discontinuous conduction [[note-3973e022]]. A team can simulate

recommendations.section: ## 6. Executing and Documenting the Project (### Make results measurable)
recommendations.current: Examples include cutoff frequency and attenuation for filters, efficiency and ripple for converters, accuracy and latency for TinyML, S11 and gain for antennas, and pipeline CPI or maximum clock frequency for processors.
recommendations.recommended:
Examples by project type:

| Project type | Quantitative targets to state and measure |
|---|---|
| Filters | Cutoff frequency, attenuation |
| Converters | Efficiency, ripple |
| TinyML | Accuracy, latency |
| Antennas | S11, gain |
| Processors | Pipeline CPI or maximum clock frequency |
recommendations.rationale: Five project types mapped to their metrics is a lookup, and a table makes it the quick-reference students will scan when writing their R1 targets.

recommendations.section: ## 6. Executing and Documenting the Project (### Avoid the classic failure modes)
recommendations.current: The countermeasures from the same source: review requirements as a team monthly, keep a year-long schedule plus a rolling few-week plan updated weekly with explicit slack for failure, time-box routine decisions, and write a prototype test plan with photo and video documentation [[keep-the-big-picture-in-mind-the-byu-design-review]].
recommendations.recommended:
The countermeasures from the same source [[keep-the-big-picture-in-mind-the-byu-design-review]]:

- Review requirements as a team monthly.
- Keep a year-long schedule plus a rolling few-week plan, updated weekly with explicit slack for failure.
- Time-box routine decisions.
- Write a prototype test plan with photo and video documentation.
recommendations.rationale: The countermeasures mirror the bulleted failure list directly above, so matching bullet form lets readers pair each mistake with its fix.

recommendations.section: ## 3. Mini Projects vs Final-Year Major Projects
recommendations.current: A good strategy is to make the mini project a stepping stone. An LTspice filter mini project becomes the analog front end of a final-year ECG system. An FSM mini project grows into a RISC-V core. An FM receiver becomes an ADALM-Pluto digital link. Each final-year review then builds on work the student already understands.
recommendations.recommended:
A good strategy is to make the mini project a stepping stone:

- **Analog:** an LTspice filter mini project becomes the analog front end of a final-year ECG system.
- **Digital:** an FSM mini project grows into a RISC-V core.
- **Communication:** an FM receiver becomes an ADALM-Pluto digital link.

Each final-year review then builds on work the student already understands.
recommendations.rationale: Three parallel mini-to-major progressions written as short sentences read choppily; as a list with domain labels they form a scannable upgrade path.

recommendations.section: ## 6. Executing and Documenting the Project (### Avoid the classic failure modes)
recommendations.current:
- Ignoring one requirement because others seem more urgent, so the customer is disappointed.
- Ordering parts too late ("We forget to order parts early when they may take weeks to arrive").
- Leaving no time for things to fail, even though debugging unseen failures is part of the process.
- Building only one prototype, then having nothing to show after destructive testing, and not photographing it first.
- Over-researching trivial component choices.
recommendations.recommended:
- **Ignoring one requirement** because others seem more urgent, so the customer is disappointed.
- **Ordering parts too late** ("We forget to order parts early when they may take weeks to arrive").
- **Leaving no time for things to fail**, even though debugging unseen failures is part of the process.
- **Building only one prototype**, then having nothing to show after destructive testing, and not photographing it first.
- **Over-researching** trivial component choices.
recommendations.rationale: Bolding the opening phrase of each failure mode matches the bold-led checklist in Section 1 and makes the list scannable.

recommendations.section: ## 6. Executing and Documenting the Project (### Report structure that scores)
recommendations.current:
1. Problem statement and a survey of existing systems, with at least two or three published comparators.
2. Specifications with numeric targets.
3. Design alternatives considered and the reason for the chosen one.
4. Simulation results (LTspice, ModelSim, CST/HFSS, Edge Impulse) before hardware.
5. Hardware implementation, with photographs of each prototype iteration.
6. Test results against the specifications, including failures and fixes.
7. A PO mapping, covering sustainability, safety, ethics and cost as the NBA criteria expect [[national-board-of-accreditation-2]].
8. Limitations and future work, modelled on the RISC-V dissertation's explicit list of missing features [[design-and-simulate-risc-v-procesor-using-verilog]].
recommendations.recommended:
1. **Problem statement** and a survey of existing systems, with at least two or three published comparators.
2. **Specifications** with numeric targets.
3. **Design alternatives** considered and the reason for the chosen one.
4. **Simulation results** (LTspice, ModelSim, CST/HFSS, Edge Impulse) before hardware.
5. **Hardware implementation**, with photographs of each prototype iteration.
6. **Test results** against the specifications, including failures and fixes.
7. **A PO mapping**, covering sustainability, safety, ethics and cost as the NBA criteria expect [[national-board-of-accreditation-2]].
8. **Limitations and future work**, modelled on the RISC-V dissertation's explicit list of missing features [[design-and-simulate-risc-v-procesor-using-verilog]].
recommendations.rationale: Bold chapter labels turn the list into a report outline that reads at a glance.
